headline: Lindsay Clancy jury mistrial after 38-hour deliberation with lone holdout juror
body: The jury in Lindsay Clancy’s murder case couldn’t reach a unanimous verdict after 38 hours of deliberation, prompting the judge to declare a mistrial. A lone juror refused to vote not guilty by insanity, and after two re-sentences, the judge ruled by law that a mistrial was necessary. Clancy’s defense attorney Kevin Reddington argued the judge had discretion to continue deliberations, but the judge rejected the argument. The jury sent a note expressing it was 'with a heavy heart' they couldn’t reach consensus.

caption:
Jurors in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial were unable to agree on a verdict after 38 hours. One juror held out, refusing to vote not guilty by insanity. The judge declared a mistrial after two attempts to reach consensus. Clancy’s defense attorney Kevin Reddington argued the judge could have pressed on, but the judge said he was legally obligated to end the trial.
